newsitem.title: USA: Digi Intl named in class action suit.
newsitem.headline: Digi Intl named in class action suit.

text.p: A purported class action lawsuit has been filed against Digi International Inc on behalf of individuals who bought Digi stock between January 25 and December 23, 1996, lawyers for the plaintiffs said Monday.
According to the lawyers, the complaint alleges that Digi and certain company officers misrepresented and omitted information that resulted in overstated financial results and inflated stock prices.
Company officials were not available for comment.
Digi shares were off 1/2 at 9-5/8 at midday.
Digi's stock, which had traded at a high of $30, fell below $9 on December 24 after the company revised downward its fiscal 1996 earnings and forecast weaker first quarter profits.
The firms representing the plaintiffs in the suit are Wolf Popper LLP and Lockridge Grindal Nauen & Holstein PLLP.

According to the lawyers, the suit alleges Digi failed to follow generally accepted accounting principles in accounting for its investment in AetherWorks Corp. The suit also alleges that Digi failed to accrue adequate reserves to cover returns in the first three quarters of 1996.
Earlier today Digi announced the resignation of its president and chief executive, Ervin Kamm.
